title: voice-lint test suite (#56): captured-not-hand-written owner fixtures, deterministic utimesSync stamping, and the run.sh git-clone-blindness hazard QA root-caused
content:
Landed at #56 (merged b5f6f52, PR #87). test-voice-lint.sh grew from 71 to 267 cells. Three reusable testing-discipline lessons from this issue, none specific to voice-lint's own logic.

1. A CAPTURED FIXTURE BEATS A HAND-WRITTEN ONE, AND THE RULE HAS A SHARP FAILURE MODE WHEN APPLIED PARTIALLY. Every fixture record standing in for an owner-authored, task-notification, auto-compaction, or cross-session transcript entry in this suite is CAPTURED verbatim from a live transcript rather than hand-written, and each capture is pinned by an asserted present-tense fact about it (its type, its origin.kind or its absence, its isMeta, its content shape) so a future vendor change to that record shape reddens the fixture instead of quietly satisfying a stale assumption. Round 2 of this issue's own review scoped the capture rule to the NON-owner classes only (task-notification, auto-compaction, refusal, cross-session), leaving the OWNER control record as the one place a Dev was free to hand-write a fixture -- which is exactly the record that has to carry `origin` at the correct RECORD level (see architecture--voice-lint-turn-scoping.json's nesting hazard). A hand-written owner fixture with `origin` nested under `message` (the natural misreading) and an implementation that reads `record.message?.origin?.kind` (the same misreading) CANCEL: the fixture passes for the wrong reason and the suite stays green while the shipped predicate is a permanent no-op. The lesson generalises past this one field: when a capture-not-hand-write rule is scoped to 'the classes that need special handling', check whether the CONTROL record in the same fixture matrix was left out of scope, because that is precisely where an implementation bug and a fixture bug are most likely to be mirror images of each other and cancel silently.

2. DETERMINISTIC MTIME STAMPING: node's fs.utimesSync, NEVER shell `touch -t`. Round 1 of this issue's spec banned `touch -t` for new fixtures without naming a working spelling, which would have let a Dev reach for the obvious bash idiom and ship a test that passes on their own machine and fails in CI (or vice versa) for two independent reasons: BSD touch (macOS, the typical author machine) has no `-d @<epoch>` form that GNU touch (ubuntu-latest CI) does, and `touch -t` takes a LOCAL-clock value while this project's transcript timestamps are UTC ISO, so a fixture mixing the two measures the runner's timezone rather than the intended offset (measured: `touch -t 202608221341` produced a 17:41Z mtime on a UTC-4 machine). The in-tree idiom, already established at validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:942,1075,1171 before this issue and now also used in test-voice-lint.sh, is `utimesSync(file, ms / 1000, ms / 1000)`, paired with a read-back assertion that the applied stamp lands within a stated tolerance of the intended epoch, so a silent no-op stamp is named at the point it happened rather than reddening a distant, unrelated-looking cell. NOTE also recorded here because it bounds the mtime-based freshness model generally: utimesSync moves mtime but NOT ctime, so any future freshness composition that folds in ctime would make every utimesSync-stamped fixture in this style read fresh regardless of its intended mtime -- ctime-based staleness requires a real wall-clock sleep to construct honestly, which is why this suite deliberately does not use it (see decisions/declared-bounded-residual-over-forced-mechanical-fix.json for the ruling this fed).

3. THE run.sh GIT-CLONE-BLINDNESS-TO-UNCOMMITTED-CHANGES HAZARD, root-caused by QA during this issue's Phase 4 panel and filed non-blocking to #91 rather than fixed inline (deferred, not silently dropped -- the deferral itself is recorded here per the evidence-discipline rule that a deferral is an action). During Dev's implementation, a run.sh execution concurrent with an in-flight git commit reported one unnamed suite FAILED with a truncated log; two Phase 4 panel members independently root-caused it via two DIFFERENT mechanisms and only one was the actual cause of THIS incident: DevOps reproduced a plausible mid-write-file-read race in isolation, but QA found the ACTUAL cause specific to this repo's test suite -- test-issue17-integration.sh's AC41(c) CLONES the repo and runs the suite INSIDE that clone, which is structurally blind to any uncommitted working-tree state, so Dev's mid-implementation uncommitted diff got tested via the clone (which saw the LAST COMMIT, not the working tree) and failed exactly as its own commit-time diff would predict. This is a real, reproducible test-harness gap: any integration test in this project that clones the repo to get a clean copy will silently test stale state whenever it runs against an uncommitted working tree, and the failure it produces looks exactly like a real regression rather than a staleness artifact. Filed to #91 rather than fixed in this issue: the remediation (name which suite failed in run.sh's own output; make the clone-based integration test either commit-aware or explicitly document that it only ever validates the last commit) is out of scope for a voice-lint turn-scoping fix and belongs with whoever owns run.sh and test-issue17-integration.sh next. A second run.sh observability nit was filed alongside it: run.sh's own output does not name which suite failed, which is why this incident took two independent root-cause investigations instead of one.
